_comment: Provenance manifest for the Camp Kanawana visual archive. Every identified pre-2016 image gets an entry here BEFORE the image file lands, so provenance and rights are recorded. When an image is added to this directory, set status='acquired' and fill 'filename'. Canadian copyright note: photographs created before 1949 are generally public domain in Canada (and most pre-1972 published works), so the early archival images below are safely displayable. Photo-integration batch 'photodownloads-2026-06-29' added 2026-07-02: 234 images filed from three delivered archives (Concordia historical album, dining-hall plaque album, physical-artifact/art scans). See project-docs/research-log.md.

images.title: Kanawana from the Water
images.source: The Gas-Bag Extra, Volume 13 Number 1 (1923), p. 2
images.rights: Published 1923 -- public domain in Canada.
images.notes: The camp shoreline from the lake: a tent above the beach and a line of boats or canoes drawn up along the shore.

images.title: Dining Pavilion, Kamp Kanawana
images.source: The Gas-Bag Extra, Volume 13 Number 1 (1923), p. 2
images.rights: Published 1923 -- public domain in Canada.
images.notes: A large log building with a deep overhanging roof and an upper rail or gallery, boys along its front. The 1988 facilities table dates the dining hall and kitchen to 1919.

images.title: Kamp Kanawana Pictorial Review
images.source: The Gas-Bag Extra, Volume 13 Number 1 (1923), p. 2
images.source_ref: Internet Archive item the-gas-bag-extra-vol-13-no-1, leaf n1
images.rights: Published 1923 -- public domain in Canada. Credit the YMCA of Montreal fonds, digitized by Concordia University Records Management and Archives.
images.notes: Seven halftones with blackletter captions -- Stories around the Fire, Dining Pavilion, Senior Tent-site, A popular Spot, Next?, Basketry Instruction, Wrestling Class -- plus a shoreline panorama captioned 'Kanawana from the Water'. Found 2026-09-06 while fetching this issue's page image for the M. E. Williams cups table (p_261). Invisible to text search: the captions are blackletter set inside the plate and the OCR read only three.

images.title: Camp Club House, Lake St. Joseph
images.caption_on_original: CAMP CLUB HOUSE, LAKE ST. JOSEPH
images.source: YMCA of Montreal, 'Men of Montreal': Fifty-Third Annual Report and Summer Camp Number, 1904 -- front cover
images.rights: Halftone published 1904 -- public domain in Canada. Credit the YMCA of Montreal fonds, digitized by Concordia University Records Management and Archives.
images.notes: The Log Club House completed September 1898, photographed for the cover of the 1904 report. A dozen or more boys and young men on the veranda, the steps and the path; a canvas blind let down at the left end of the veranda; the lake beyond. The full cover is filed alongside as 1904-men-of-montreal-summer-camp-number-cover.jpg. Found 2026-09-06 by ranking the item's djvu pages by word count and looking at the sparsest -- the caption sweep of the cached OCR missed it because the OCR runs the caption into the cover text.

images.title: The Association Summer Camp, Lake St. Joseph
images.caption_on_original: THE ASSOCIATION SUMMER CAMP, LAKE ST. JOSEPH.
images.source: YMCA of Montreal, Annual Report for the year ending 30 April 1899, p. 13 (facing the President's and Secretary's signatures)
images.source_ref: Internet Archive item sgw-ymca-annual-report-1899, leaf n14
images.rights: Halftone published 1899 -- public domain in Canada. Credit the YMCA of Montreal fonds, digitized by Concordia University Records Management and Archives.
images.notes: THE EARLIEST KNOWN PHOTOGRAPH OF THE CAMP THIS PROJECT'S HISTORY BEGINS WITH, four or five seasons after the first. Found 2026-09-06 by reading the report's page images: the OCR preserves the caption but not the plate, so no text search this project ever ran could see it. Cropped from the page scan at archive.org/download/sgw-ymca-annual-report-1899/page/n14_w1600.jpg (that endpoint needs a Referer header and -L).

images.title: Letter from Prime Minister Pierre Elliott Trudeau on the opening of Kamp Kanawana's new recreational building
images.caption_on_original: I am happy to send my greetings and congratulations to all campers and staff of Kamp Kanawana as you officially open your new recreational building. / Pierre Elliott Trudeau, Prime Minister — Premier Ministre
images.source: Operator photograph of the framed original held at Camp Kanawana
images.rights: Crown copyright, Government of Canada, 1978. Photograph of the framed original supplied by the operator. Reproduced here as a documentary record; not cleared for redistribution.
images.notes: CROPPED ABOVE THE DATELINE. Use img_trudeau_letter_1978_full for the complete sheet. This image is a closer read of the body text, and its crop caused this project to record the letter as undated for several hours. See f_4834.
